before_results.readmission: The positive class represents patients readmitted within 30 days. I consider missing a patient at risk of readmission more concerning than a false alarm because it could mean losing an opportunity for early intervention, discharge planning, or additional follow-up. While false positives can increase staff workload and resource utilization, I would prioritize identifying patients who may benefit from additional support.
before_results.diabetes: The positive class represents patients with diabetes. I would prioritize reducing missed positive cases because identifying these patients earlier could support additional testing, appropriate treatment, and better long-term management. False positives remain important because they can create unnecessary testing, additional costs, and patient anxiety, but I believe the consequences of delayed identification are generally more significant in a screening setting.

recommendations.readmission: My initial preference is a model that balances sensitivity and precision while prioritizing the identification of patients at risk of readmission. I would consider a lower decision threshold if the additional patients identified justify the increased number of false alarms. However, I would not recommend a specific model or threshold until reviewing its test performance, including sensitivity, precision, and false negatives.
recommendations.diabetes: For diabetes screening, I would favor a model with stronger sensitivity, provided its false-positive rate remains manageable. A threshold below 0.50 may be appropriate if it identifies substantially more patients who would otherwise be missed. My final recommendation will depend on the test results and whether the additional screening burden is reasonable.

design.design_choice: I chose to emphasize sensitivity, false negatives, and confusion matrices rather than presenting accuracy as the primary measure of model performance. From a healthcare operations perspective, I believe it is important to understand how model errors affect patient identification, clinical workflows, and resource utilization. I also wanted the interface to remain straightforward so users could compare results without unnecessary visual distractions.
design.ai_turned_down: I chose not to treat the model with the highest accuracy as the automatic recommendation. Although accuracy provides a useful overall measure, I wanted the evaluation to reflect the consequences of missed cases, false alarms, and performance on new patients. I also preferred a more restrained dashboard design rather than adding visual elements that would distract from the clinical analysis.
